title: Institutional Portfolio Management
subtitle: How pensions, endowments and sovereign funds actually run money, and which of their habits a $500,000 account can borrow.
what_you_learn: Name the liability behind every institutional portfolio (CalPERS, Yale, Harvard, Norway's GPFG) and derive the required return from it
Write an investment policy statement with liability-derived objectives, hard constraints, policy bands and a review rule
Build a strategic allocation from published capital-market assumptions and compute its expected return, volatility and risk contributions
Judge benchmarks, tracking error, active share and fee per unit of active share, and read the evidence on closet indexing and 2-and-20
Rebalance by rule, budget liquidity for a 2008-style shock, and measure results the GIPS way: time-weighted, net of fees, with Brinson attribution
Separate the five institutional habits that scale down to an individual from the five that do not, and prove it with a graded capstone IPS
